artworks.title: Melampus healing the daughters of Proetus
artworks.description: A Lucanian red-figure nestoris in Naples stages Melampus curing the Proetids — the maddened daughters of King Proetus of Tiryns. The vase is the chief ancient image of the household crisis that cost Proetus a third of Argos to the seer and his brother Bias.

artworks.title: Bellerophon and Stheneboea (Antakya Four Seasons mosaic)
artworks.description: The Antakya Four Seasons mosaic shows Bellerophon with Stheneboea (Anteia) — Proetus' queen, whose false accusation sends the hero to Lycia with the sealed letter. Proetus' court is the hinge of the Bellerophon cycle even when the king himself stays off-panel.

popCulture.title: Bellerophon
popCulture.description: Iliad 6 and later mythographers make Proetus the Tirynthian host who, deceived by Stheneboea, packs Bellerophon off to Iobates with a death-letter — the king as reluctant would-be murderer.

popCulture.title: Tiryns
popCulture.description: Proetus fortifies Tiryns with Cyclopean walls after sharing Argos with Acrisius — the king whose city still stands as the stone twin of Mycenae.

popCulture.title: Proetus
popCulture.description: Twin of Acrisius, king of Tiryns, father of the Proetids, host of Bellerophon — the Argive ruler whose household drives two of Greece's great cycles.
